title: Boolean Logic: Exactly One
hints: `Bool` isn't a number in Swift, so you can't add them up directly.
Put the three flags in an array and count how many are `true`.
jsBridge: JS has truthiness: `true + true === 2` and `if (count)` works. Swift's `Bool` is not a number and nothing is truthy, so `if count` doesn't compile. You write `count > 0`, or count with `filter { $0 }.count`.

compass.q: List three JS truthiness bugs (`0`, `""`, `NaN`) that Swift's `Bool` rules make impossible. Is anything lost?
`a != b` works as XOR for two Bools. Why doesn't it generalise to "exactly one of three"?
A settings screen has three mutually exclusive toggles. Would you model them as three Bools or as one enum? What does the enum prevent?
`Bool.toggle()` is a mutating method. Why is that nicer in SwiftUI (`isOn.toggle()`) than `isOn = !isOn`?
